name: a retrospectively-dated conflicting attribute is never buried as history — the newest statement wins
description: Adversarial: note A asserts Tomas's birthday is 1991-08-03. Note B, captured a week LATER, gives a CONFLICTING birthday 1990-04-12 but is phrased retrospectively, so its temporal is the OLDER of the two. The property: the newest STATEMENT is live, and the old VALIDITY does not bury it as closed history behind the value it disputes. ⟲ The dates were swapped when this was re-measured, and what that established is worth recording precisely, because two earlier readings of it were wrong. As first written, note B's validity was the NEWER of the two, so the fixture never posed the retrospective shape its name claims. Swapped, it does. But it still does not DISCRIMINATE an ordering key, and no fixture could: the attribute arm never compares the candidate against a head at all — the candidate always lands active and supersedes — so validity-vs-reported_at decides only which head is CITED as the conflicting row and whose confidence the low-confidence floor compares against. Measured directly against decide(): a candidate whose validity is older than the head's still goes active and supersedes. So this scenario is a REGRESSION GUARD, not a discriminator: it pins that a retrospectively-dated value is not demoted, and it would fail if someone later made validity pick the winner. ⟲ REWRITTEN before that for the owner's ruling on AGENT_INGEST_REWRITE §8 O15, which changed the disposition and not the property. It used to assert that BOTH birthdays end pending_review and NEITHER is live — the behaviour the owner overruled, because holding both left the key permanently contested with nothing on the box able to retire either row, so Tomas served no birthday at all. Now the newest statement is ACTIVE and the older one is superseded and CHAINED to it, kept as history. Split detection still ignores validity entirely (a backdated wrong birthday is still a split signal), and the split remains an answer the owner may give when asked. ONE CHANNEL (AGENT_INGEST_REWRITE R1b): the harness IS the note conversation and its write path files no review card — decide() reports back in the tool result and the AGENT settles it, which since O15 means asking the owner which value is right. So the card count is 0 and the ROW STATUSES above are the whole assertion: decide()'s authority over what LANDS is untouched, only who is told moved.

steps.body: An old record from years ago lists Tomas's birthday as April 12, 1990.
